premises: Original-coordinate rank-two hub/leaf cross geometry with full-column-rank C.
Arbitrary symmetric within-leaf block D; no probabilistic moment/support assumptions enter the deterministic theorem.
For the probabilistic applications, independent original cap-one coordinates are retained and only completed source-pinned Fourier/Pluecker theorems are used.
theorem_summary: Let Delta=sqrt(det(C^T C)), ell_k=c_k^T(C^T C)^(-1)c_k, q=max ell_k<1, and Gamma_k be the third singular-volume of the singleton-augmented physical cross block. Then Gamma_k^2=Delta^2(1-ell_k)delta_k^2 and Delta^(-1)(sum Gamma_k^2)^(1/2) <= inf_{S symmetric,Lambda diagonal}||D-CSC^T-Lambda||_F <= sqrt(2)/(Delta sqrt(1-q))(sum Gamma_k^2)^(1/2).
counterexample_summary: For flat orthonormal Walsh C=[c1,c2] and u, A_N=[[0,C^T],[C,u u^T]] has spectrum {-1,-1,1,1,1}; max singleton Gamma tends to zero but sum Gamma_k^2 tends to one and the distance to C Sym_2 C^T plus diagonal stays order one. This refutes max-singleton stability only, not QFORM.

partner_result_applied.actual_inequality: On the Walsh family, max literal physical 3x3 cross determinant is 4/N^2, so ||p_Q||_inf <=3(4/N^2)^(-1/3); at N=256 this is 76.195250494473555.

newest_source_applied.actual_inequality: For singleton augmented M_k with E3(M_k)=Gamma_k^2 and row-volume marginals <=1/2, q=1 gives ||p_Q||_inf <=3e Gamma_k^(-1/3).

unresolved_implication: QFORM-RANK2-AGGREGATE-CURVATURE-DECOMPOSITION-v1: convert order-one aggregate stability defect into a determinant-distributed transverse curvature packet, a universal rank-at-least-three volume exit, or a finite-core/high-leverage paid exit, without discarding residual quadratic phase as a small random error.
